overview: The SIM800L gives a microcontroller access to the actual cellular network — SMS, phone calls, and basic GPRS data — using a regular SIM card, completely independent of any WiFi network. It's controlled over UART with AT commands, similar in spirit to a Bluetooth module, but with a power requirement that catches almost every beginner off guard: while idle it draws a modest ~20mA, but the instant it transmits (registering on the network, sending an SMS) it can spike to 2A for brief bursts, which a microcontroller's onboard 5V regulator or a small USB power bank cannot supply — undersized power is the number one reason these modules seem to 'randomly reset' or 'not turn on.'
simpleSummary: A module that gives a microcontroller access to the cell network — texting, calling, basic data.

specifications.operatingVoltage: 3.4V - 4.4V (NOT 5V — needs its own regulated supply, not a microcontroller's 5V rail)
specifications.currentDraw: ~20mA idle, up to 2A in brief transmit bursts
specifications.simCard: Requires a micro-SIM card with active service

pinMap.name: VCC
pinMap.function: Power input — needs a dedicated supply capable of 2A bursts, not a microcontroller's onboard regulator.
pinMap.gotcha: The single most common SIM800L failure: powering it from an Arduino's 5V/3.3V pin, which cannot supply transmit-burst current, causing the module to brown out and reset right when it tries to connect.

pinMap.name: RXD
pinMap.gotcha: Not reliably 5V tolerant — use a level shifter or voltage divider from a 5V microcontroller's TX pin.

pinMap.name: NET
pinMap.function: Connection point for an external antenna (often a small spring/helical antenna soldered here or a nearby connector).
pinMap.gotcha: Weak or missing antenna connection is the second most common 'won't register on the network' cause after power issues.

useCases.title: Remote SMS alert system
useCases.scenario: Send an SMS alert when a sensor threshold is crossed, with no WiFi/internet infrastructure needed.

useCases.title: GPS tracker with cellular reporting
useCases.scenario: Combine with a GPS module to periodically report location via SMS or GPRS data.

useCases.title: Remote equipment monitoring in areas without WiFi
useCases.scenario: Cellular connectivity for agricultural, remote industrial, or off-grid monitoring projects.

oftenConfusedWith: ESP32 (WiFi only, no cellular network access)
oftenUpgradedTo: 4G/LTE Cat-M modules for faster data and better network coverage as 2G/3G networks are phased out in many regions
